Investigating phishing attacks

Last updated
Data required

Test introduction: analysts receive reports of suspicious attachments and need to scope the campaign.

Attackers commonly use spearphishing attachments (T1566.001) to gain access.

Prerequisites

Data

  • Email gateway logs
  • Google: Workspace

Software

  • Splunk Enterprise Security
  • Splunk Security Essentials

How to use Splunk software for this use case

Follow these test steps:

  1. Install the add-on.
    • Use the search head.
    • Restart if prompted.
  2. Run the searches below.
FieldMeaning
senderEnvelope sender address
file_nameAttachment name
► Click to see the search
index=email sourcetype="gws:gmail" attachment=*
| stats count BY sender, file_name
| where count > 5

Search explanation

index=emailSearch the email index.

Correlate with endpoint data

| tstats count FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Processes WHERE Processes.process_name="outlook.exe" BY Processes.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| lookup asset_lookup dest OUTPUT owner

Run this on the host:

sudo systemctl restart splunk

Tip: test note inside the article.

Dashboards

  • Phishing overview dashboard

Possible outcomes

Faster scoping of phishing campaigns and fewer compromised accounts.
